title: A Held Fill That Straddles the Deductible Boundary on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
Where the member has already been paying at the deductible stage, the share a held fill leaves them on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan is worked out at the boundary rather than from the cost share alone.

1. Where at least 1 fill stands paid on the pharmacy record at the deductible stage and the price the cost share is taken from is more than the deductible still to be met, the fill is split at the boundary: the member pays the deductible still to be met, together with the cost share for the fill in the proportion the price above the deductible bears to the whole price, that proportional part being rounded to two decimal places before it is added.
2. Where at least 1 fill stands paid on the pharmacy record at the deductible stage and the price the cost share is taken from is at most the deductible still to be met, the member pays the whole of that price.
3. Where no fill stands paid on the pharmacy record at the deductible stage, the member pays the cost share for the fill.

| Fills standing paid at the deductible stage | The price against the deductible still to be met | What the payment stage leaves the member |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 or more | price greater than the deductible still to be met | the deductible still to be met, plus the proportional part of the cost share |
| 1 or more | price equal to the deductible still to be met | the whole of that price |
| 1 or more | price less than the deductible still to be met | the whole of that price |
| none | any | the cost share for the fill |

A price standing exactly equal to the deductible still to be met falls in the second rule, not the first.

## Worked on hypothetical figures

Take a deductible still to be met of 60.00 USD, a price the cost share is taken from of 200.00 USD, and a cost share for the fill of 25.00 USD, with 2 fills standing paid at the deductible stage.

- The price of 200.00 USD is above the deductible still to be met, so the fill is split.
- The price above the deductible is 140.00 USD, which bears to the whole price of 200.00 USD the proportion of seven tenths.
- The cost share of 25.00 USD in that proportion is 17.50 USD, which is the proportional part rounded to two decimal places.
- The member is left with 60.00 USD together with 17.50 USD, that is 77.50 USD.

Take instead a deductible still to be met of 260.00 USD against the same price of 200.00 USD: the price is below it, and the member is left with the whole 200.00 USD. Take a record on which no fill stands paid at the deductible stage: the member is left with the cost share of 25.00 USD.
